object_description: linear school building composed of three diagonally shifted volumes
design_condition: The three connected volumes are placed centrally and shifted to recede from the trees and railway, form a head toward the intersection, and divide the surrounding open space into distinct outdoor areas.

positive.statement: The shifted volumes fit clearly into the surrounding development while still reading as a new public building.

position.rationale: Three diagonally shifted volumes are strongly visible in plan and elevations.

positive.statement: The staggered volume divides the narrow open space and creates more spacious outdoor areas rather than residual space.

position.rationale: The zigzag plan visibly divides the surrounding open space into larger pockets.

positive.statement: The outdoor spaces provide different play and lounge areas on all sides of the building.

position.rationale: Multiple exterior pockets are distributed along the building’s shifted sides.

positive.statement: The internal connections between group rooms and main rooms allow cross-class teaching methods.

position.rationale: Internal links are not visible; the marker follows the central connected volume.

positive.statement: The main uses of the basic levels are sensibly arranged and easily accessible for smaller children.

position.rationale: The accessible lower-level zone is anchored to the low-rise sampled envelope.

positive.statement: The project provides a contemporary answer and connects with the surrounding context.

position.rationale: The stepped linear silhouette visibly provides a contemporary contextual identity.

negative.statement: The number of outdoor spaces makes it difficult to maintain an overview.

position.rationale: Several separated exterior pockets are evident around the zigzag footprint.

negative.statement: The furniture appears randomly distributed, and delivery at the street junction is problematic.

position.rationale: The junction-side edge is used for the uncertain delivery and furniture-related site issue.

negative.statement: The difference in height of the existing trees in the entrance area was not taken into account.

position.rationale: Tree height is not encoded distinctly; the entrance-edge landscape is approximated.

negative.statement: The children enter a relatively narrow break room with access stairs.

position.target: narrow break room with access stairs
position.rationale: The interior room and stairs are approximated within the lower central volume.

negative.statement: The project creates conflicts inside, including a walk-through cloakroom and prominently located toilets.

position.rationale: Internal conflicts are anchored to the connected middle portion of the building.

negative.statement: The project is not convincing enough in its urban setting, pavilion legibility and expression.

position.rationale: The whole stepped form is visible, though its contextual reading remains a broad judgment.

negative.statement: The high glass proportion causes winter comfort losses and expected losses of light and views when blinds are closed.

position.rationale: Facade performance is assigned to the exposed south elevation where glazing effects would occur.

negative.statement: The external treatment and glass content make compliance with the primary energy requirements difficult.

position.rationale: Energy compliance concerns are anchored to the sampled outer facade envelope.
